title: Hypergraph Representation Learning with Hyperlink Random Effects
claim: Heterogeneous multi-way interactions arise from latent group-level effects combined with entity embeddings, which together generate the observed hyperlinks.
layout: 4 columns, left-to-right, dotted arrows linking effects to sets to hypergraph
description: A left-to-right toy example in four labeled columns. On the left, 'Random effects' shows three overlapping bell curves (red, orange, teal), a Gaussian-mixture sketch. Dotted arrows fan out from the curves to six colored horizontal bars under 'Patient latent characteristics', one bar per patient. Dotted arrows lead from each bar to a 'Patient profiles' column, where each row is a set of numbered colored circles (symptoms 1–5), such as {1,2,5} or {2,3}. Two gray dashed boxes, 'Symptom latent characteristics' and 'Symptom degree parameters', sit over the arrows. On the right, 'Hypergraph' draws the five symptom nodes inside overlapping ellipses that stand for hyperlinks. A 'Symptoms' label points to the nodes with dotted arrows. Gray label boxes with orange borders head each column.
caption: Illustration of hypergraph representation learning with hyperlink random effects using a patient-profile toy example. The data are represented as a symptom co-occurrence hypergraph with five nodes, corresponding to symptoms, and six observed hyperlinks, corresponding to symptom sets observed in individual patient profiles. Each symptom is assigned a latent embedding and degree parameter. To capture patient-level heterogeneity, each profile is assigned a hyperlink random-effect embedding representing latent patient characteristics that drive profile formation.
abstract: Hypergraphs record multi-way interactions among entities. Extracting information from the combinatorial structure underlying observed multi-way interactions is a central task in many real-world problems. Existing methods face several limitations. First, many deep architectures for hypergraphs do not explicitly exploit the potential low-rank structure, which can sacrifice parsimony and interpretability in the learned representations. Second, many low-rank-based methods operate on tensor representations, which typically require hyperlinks to have uniform sizes and thus limit their applicability to general hypergraphs with non-uniform hyperlink sizes. Third, many methods ignore the fact that hyperlinks often arise from heterogeneous mechanisms. For example, medical symptoms may co-occur in the profiles of patients with very different conditions, and such heterogeneity should be incorporated into the learning process. In this work, we develop a general framework for hypergraph representation learning using hyperlink random effects while exploiting the low-rank structure in hypergraphs. The proposed framework accommodates latent heterogeneity in hyperlink formation while preserving entity interaction patterns. We establish identifiability of the model parameters and theoretical guarantees of representation-level recovery under this framework. The framework allows flexible specifications for the hyperlink random effects; in this paper, we study three choices: categorical, Gaussian mixture, and score-based effects, and develop corresponding estimation algorithms. Through simulation studies, we demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in recovering latent structure and capturing heterogeneous interaction patterns. Empirical studies on real-world hypergraph datasets further illustrate the practical utility of our approach.
